reviews.review:
Needs a few patches for all the random bugs, but otherwise amazing game, the narrative and the illustrations were fantastic and I really enjoyed the characters. Unfortunately I had multiple softlocks, many cosmetic glitches like duplicating items, and accidentally doing events out of sequence. The game is about 20% visual novel, 80% interactive puzzle game, one run takes about 70 minutes blind, but you could put more than 4 hours into the game, depending how many endings you want to see, there are several, and I would say they are very rewarding with different conclusions and art panels.

Even though I liked the thought process behind the puzzles in terms of their metaphors and contextualizing the characters, mechanically they were somewhat poorly implemented, it's hard to explain - they are not as intuitive as they should be. Still, I think the puzzles were very creative on paper, some areas were more logical than others. Don't get me wrong, I think what you doing is perfectly fine, I like how the stages are designed specifically for the character, so all of the puzzles contribute to that specific scene, it's just that it's easy to get ahead of the hints, and the game is not always giving a good feedback. Your character is presented with various moral choices during the game that are specific to 2 savory characters, and you will choose to align yourself with them, or perhaps leave them behind, that is kind of the general idea of the story.

During the playthrough you will have a choice between saving 0 and 2 characters which will impact the endings that you can access, as well as some of the events in the middle, adding some theory crafting when it comes to figuring out what you could do differently. By itself I think the game has a decent amount of choice variety, however, picking a wrong route does not block puzzles for those different endings, so you might run yourself into a corner, even though you have no access to a certain item to make progress.

[h1] Pros: [/h1]

(+) Several endings with multiple important choices during the game based on which characters you kill or bring with you, kinda has that nice theory crafting, figuring out what you can do differently

(+) The art panels and level design were extremely good for the most part (the only one I didn't like was the first stage). I like how you designed those levels for those specific characters and their personal issues, including the puzzles that were part of the painful events they experienced 

(+) All of the characters had some depth to them that was slowly shown during the narrative, having good mystery, interesting endings, and good character development, with a few unique ideas

[h1] Feedback: [/h1]

- some of the routes that you can take in this game can block your from getting certain endings which is fine, but they don't remove some puzzle elements that are associated with those endings, so you could be trying to solve an unsolvable puzzle for 2 hours because you have items in the inventory that you can't use.

- there is something wrong with the dialogue/translation between red and black dress, if feels like you have to trigger performance twice and talk twice, but reading the dialogue it feels like you reading the same thing, confusing for a player, not sure exactly if it's a bug or translation problem

- loading the game occasionally corrupts specific puzzles or navigation, making it impossible to finish

- the game was really buggy at the time of me playing, hopefully it slowly gets fixed. I had multiple softlocks, constant issues with puzzles giving copies of the items I already used, and other issues with interactive elements, such as not having consistent interactions or hotspots, sometimes confusing the game if you get ahead of it. A few achievements did not work for me as well. (I'll just post those bugs in the forum, so I don't clutter this review)

- the translation probably could use a little work

[b] Overall Thoughts: 7/10 (I would say 9/10 if it gets fixed properly) [/b]

Loved the game.... but I just run into a lot of technical issues, and I also think the puzzles maybe could be a bit streamlined so you can't get ahead of the hints, or maybe removing some dialogue parts once they are no longer useful, otherwise it's very easy to waste time probing the puzzles. The art panel were really good, I know some games with 10K reviews that are not this pretty, and the story actually had good character development, with multiple compelling player choices during the playthrough. 

[code]Niche, obscure and underrated games: http://store.steampowered.com/curator/31294838-Hidden-Gem-Discovery/ [/code]
